title: The One With The Nap Partners

jokes.text: Monica reveals the 'best part' of her maid-of-honor plan is that she doesn't have to decide
jokes.setup: Monica builds up 'the best part' of her rotating maid-of-honor plan with excitement
jokes.punchline: The best part is simply that she doesn't have to make the decision herself
jokes.explanation: Classic Monica move — her controlling, type-A personality ironically makes her want to avoid this one decision entirely. The misdirection works because the audience expects a heartfelt reason but gets naked self-interest instead.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Please let it be me.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Please let it be me.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You both can't be maid of honor.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: What if we share the position?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, like co-maids of honor!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's not a thing.

jokes.text: Rachel begins an elaborate toast while Monica is still waiting to hear who the maid of honor is
jokes.setup: Monica needs an answer about her maid of honor; Rachel starts a sincere, flowery toast
jokes.punchline: Monica flatly cuts in: 'Really not deciding.'
jokes.explanation: Good use of Rachel's oblivious self-indulgence contrasted with Monica's impatience. The cutoff is well-timed and Monica's deadpan 'Really not deciding' lands as a crisp button.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I love you both so much, and I just want you to know that whatever happens, I'm here for you.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, yeah, that's great. So anyway, can we order food? I'm starving.

jokes.text: Stranger overhears Monica is marrying Chandler Bing and says 'Good luck!' with ominous weight
jokes.setup: A stranger interrupts to offer what sounds like a warm congratulations
jokes.punchline: Her 'Good luck' is clearly a warning, not a pleasantry — implying Chandler is a disaster to marry
jokes.explanation: The joke is economical and structurally clean — same words, opposite meanings. Monica's oblivious 'What a nice lady' is a perfect button. It plants a mystery (who is she?) that pays off later, earning a rewatch bonus.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God, I'm gonna be a maid of honor! I'm gonna be a maid of honor! I'm gonna be a maid of honor!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: But, um, not to diminish anyone else's moment, because you're all gonna be great maids of honor too.

jokes.text: Monica responds to the ominous 'Good luck' with 'Oh, and good luck to you too! What a nice lady.'
jokes.setup: The stranger's 'Good luck' is clearly a warning that Monica is oblivious to
jokes.punchline: Monica cheerfully reciprocates and calls her 'a nice lady'
jokes.explanation: Monica's total obliviousness is the joke. The audience has already decoded the warning while Monica beams. Her sincerity makes it funnier.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Wait, so you're saying you just want us to decide because you don't want to make the choice?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No, that's not... okay, yes. Yes, that's exactly it.

jokes.text: Joey rents Die Hard 2 but it is actually Die Hard 1 again. 'Well, we'll watch it a second time and it's Die Hard 2.'
jokes.setup: Joey proposes a double feature and says he got Die Hard 2
jokes.punchline: It's the same tape — Die Hard 1 — and Joey's solution is simply to call it Die Hard 2 on the second viewing
jokes.explanation: Peak Joey logic — the solution is so internally consistent within Joey's worldview that it's both absurd and completely believable. The deadpan delivery of 'And?' when challenged makes it even better. Strong character integration: only Joey could arrive at this conclusion with total sincerity.

dialogue.speaker: Stranger
dialogue.line: Good luck marrying Chandler.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Stranger
dialogue.line: No, I mean GOOD luck. You're gonna NEED it.

jokes.text: Ross doesn't yell 'Die Hard!' with Joey — he has plans — and Joey responds: 'Well, John McClane had plans.'
jokes.setup: Ross declines to stay for the double feature, saying he has plans
jokes.punchline: Joey invokes John McClane as a moral authority on overcoming plans
jokes.explanation: Beautifully economical — four words that reframe a movie character as a life coach. The logic is absurd but delivered with total Joey sincerity. High quotability because it works out of context. The structure (excuse → fictional counterexample) is clean and snappy.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Joey, you rented Die Hard 1 again. We've all seen this one.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No, no, no. This is Die Hard 2. I watched the first one yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That doesn't make it the sequel.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Sure it does. First time I watch it, that's Die Hard 1. Second time I watch it, that's Die Hard 2.

jokes.text: Ross's aside: 'I want to leave before Joey gets all worked up and starts calling everybody bitch.'
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to exit before the Die Hard enthusiasm escalates
jokes.punchline: His specific fear is Joey calling everyone 'bitch' — a very specific, very believable Joey trait
jokes.explanation: The joke works because it's immediately confirmed. The specificity ('calling everybody bitch') elevates it from a generic Joey-is-dumb joke to something that feels observed and earned. Gets a rewatch bonus because the payoff is instant.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Die Hard!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Die Hard!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Chandler?

jokes.text: Joey immediately calls Ross 'bitch' the moment he walks out the door
jokes.setup: Ross just predicted Joey would call everyone 'bitch'
jokes.punchline: Joey calls Ross 'bitch' the instant he's out the door, confirming the prediction with perfect timing
jokes.explanation: A textbook setup-payoff where the callback is immediate and perfectly timed. The comedy isn't just the word — it's that Ross's exit line is INSTANTLY validated with zero delay. The structure here is nearly flawless: plant, exit, bang. One of the tightest jokes in the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No, no, no. You can't leave. What would John McClane do?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: John McClane wouldn't bail on his friends. He'd stay and fight.

jokes.text: Phoebe suggests she might marry Ross or Joey as examples of uncertain future husbands
jokes.setup: Rachel argues she should be Monica's maid of honor because Phoebe's future wedding is uncertain
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's examples of who she might marry are Ross and Joey — the group's most absurd pairings
jokes.explanation: Light laugh — the joke is in the specific names chosen, which are both absurd in-universe. Rachel's gasp sells it. Not a big joke but functional character comedy.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You need to stop getting so worked up and calling people 'bitch.'

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I'm not worked up, bitch!

jokes.text: Phoebe trails off in her argument and Rachel says 'I guess that was it.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe passionately says 'Please let me finish' and then has nothing more to say
jokes.punchline: Rachel's flat 'I guess that was it' acknowledging Phoebe's argument fizzled out
jokes.explanation: Nicely structured — the 'Please let me finish' builds expectation of a great argument, and the total void that follows is the punchline. Rachel's deadpan observation is perfectly economical.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm gonna marry one of you guys someday.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No you're not.

jokes.text: Phoebe says she'll marry someone 'better than Chandler', and Rachel goes 'Pfft'
jokes.setup: Phoebe reassures Rachel she'll marry someone good
jokes.punchline: She adds 'better than Chandler' and Rachel's dismissive 'pfft' implies that's not hard
jokes.explanation: Light dig at Chandler that works as quick comic punctuation. Not particularly original but efficiently delivered.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Let me finish my argument.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Okay, go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: That's it.

jokes.text: Phoebe consoles Rachel by saying 'I'm gonna marry someone good. Better than Chandler.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe is trying to comfort Rachel about losing the maid-of-honor competition.
jokes.punchline: The 'comfort' includes a casual dig at Chandler, which Phoebe seems to intend as genuine encouragement.
jokes.explanation: Mild but functional. Phoebe insulting Chandler while trying to be nice is consistent with her character's social obliviousness. The 'Pfft' reaction from the other side sells it. Doesn't quite reach the heights of her best moments.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm going to marry someone really good.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, the bar's not that high.

jokes.text: Ross and Joey both yell in shock — they've fallen asleep together on the couch
jokes.setup: Scene cuts to Ross and Joey clearly having just woken up together on the couch in an intimate position
jokes.punchline: Both men yell in mutual alarm — the visual of two grown men startled by their own closeness
jokes.explanation: The reveal of the nap situation is pure visual comedy. The mutual yelp of alarm — two men panicking about innocent physical closeness — is a strong multi-camera moment that plays well to a live audience. The B-plot's premise is established here with great economy.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: So... that was weird.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Yeah. Really weird.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I mean, we're guys. Guys don't... nap together.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Right. It was just a nap.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Just a nap.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: We should probably never speak of this again.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Agreed.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Okay, well, see you later.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah, see you.

jokes.text: Ross and Joey's awkward goodbye ritual: 'No touch. No touch.'
jokes.setup: Ross and Joey are trying to end the interaction without acknowledging the nap
jokes.punchline: Their goodbye devolves into mutually agreed 'No touch. No touch.' — actively avoiding any physical farewell
jokes.explanation: Brilliant economy — two words that capture the entire dynamic. The cringe is perfectly calibrated: they're not homophobic, they're just panicking. 'No touch. No touch.' is highly quotable and the mutual agreement makes it funnier than if only one said it. Strong rewatch value.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yippee-ki-yay! It's the best action movie ever made!

jokes.text: Chandler asks what the woman looked like; Monica says '30, dark hair, attractive.' Chandler: 'Any chance you were looking into a bright, shiny thing called a mirror?'
jokes.setup: Chandler asks Monica to describe the woman who warned her about him
jokes.punchline: He suggests Monica was looking at her own reflection — both a compliment and a deflection
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler compliment-wrapped-in-deflection. 'Bright, shiny thing called a mirror' is a little wordy but the character voice is right. It's a smooth maneuver that also reveals his anxiety about the mysterious woman.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh great, a cooking show! Finally something educational and wholesome.

dialogue.speaker: TV show
dialogue.line: And now, we'll be making a delicious casserole... at our topless carwash!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: What?!

jokes.text: Chandler claims he only dated two girls in college, 'both blond, both not attractive'
jokes.setup: Monica asks if the mystery woman is someone Chandler dated in college
jokes.punchline: Chandler's self-deprecating college romantic history — 'both not attractive' — delivered as dry fact
jokes.explanation: Light self-deprecating Chandler joke. The 'not attractive' detail is a nice specific touch — not saying they were ugly, but carefully not saying they were pretty either. Functional.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Or she could have just said 'good luck,' Chandler. That would have worked too.

jokes.text: Monica asks 'Did you break up with her?' Chandler: 'No, we're still together.' [beat] 'We went out for two summers and then I broke up with her.'
jokes.setup: Monica asks if he broke up with his camp girlfriend
jokes.punchline: Chandler deadpans 'No, we're still together' then immediately corrects himself with the actual answer after a beat
jokes.explanation: A well-constructed beat: the deadpan false answer followed by an immediate, matter-of-fact correction. Chandler's dry humor is well-deployed here. The pause between statements is where the comedy lives.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: She was beautiful, she had this incredible smile, she wished you luck.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh, so you were looking in a mirror.

jokes.text: 'Fat? I did not say fat. I said fa... Ahh.'
jokes.setup: Monica directly asks if he broke up with the girl for being fat
jokes.punchline: Chandler denies saying 'fat' while in the same breath producing the exact same incomplete non-word
jokes.explanation: The repetition escalates the original joke. His literal denial while doing the exact same thing is a clean callback. The audience is now in on the pattern.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, I went to college, Monica. I dated... I dated people. It's not like I was a monk or anything. Although, let's be honest, a monk probably had better luck than I did.

jokes.text: Monica: 'You know what they say, Elephants never forget.'
jokes.setup: Chandler asks if Julie still feels bad about being dumped for her weight
jokes.punchline: Monica drops the elephant idiom — which is about memory but also inadvertently calls Julie an elephant
jokes.explanation: A genuinely clever double-meaning joke — the proverb is accurate (Julie does remember) but its elephant metaphor lands as an inadvertent additional insult. Monica may or may not intend the double meaning, which makes it funnier either way. Good economy and structure.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Did you break up with your camp girlfriend?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, we're still together. It's been 16 years, so I'm thinking maybe we should make it official.

jokes.text: Chandler, hearing Monica's elephant line, sighs: 'Seriously, good luck marrying me.'
jokes.setup: The stranger's 'good luck' has been a running implication that Chandler is a bad catch
jokes.punchline: Chandler himself echoes the stranger's line, now fully agreeing with it
jokes.explanation: A satisfying callback that deepens the opening joke. Chandler's self-awareness and self-deprecation are his defining traits, so having him adopt the stranger's warning as his own is well-integrated. Rewatch bonus for the thematic connection to the opening scene.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm not fat, I'm... I'm... well, let's just say I'm not seeing my feet without a mirror.

jokes.text: Joey casually mentions Rachel was 'maid of honor for that girl downstairs' — revealing Phoebe lied
jokes.setup: Joey cheerfully congratulates Phoebe on being maid of honor, unaware of the conflict
jokes.punchline: He casually references Rachel having already done it 'for that girl downstairs' — exposing Phoebe's lie
jokes.explanation: Joey blowing up Phoebe's lie through sheer innocent obliviousness is a great use of the character. The humor is both situational and character-based — only Joey would casually detonate this bomb.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Does Julie still feel bad about the breakup?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: An elephant never forgets.

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'You see? This is exactly why you shouldn't lie.' — said to Rachel, who didn't lie
jokes.setup: Joey exposes that Rachel has been maid of honor before, contradicting Phoebe's claim
jokes.punchline: Phoebe lectures Rachel about not lying — when it was Phoebe who lied
jokes.explanation: Perfectly Phoebe — projecting her own guilt onto Rachel with complete conviction. The irony is crystal clear to the audience while Phoebe remains oblivious. Strong character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Phoebe, you're going to be my maid of honor.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God, really? That's so exciting!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Yeah, well, there's just one thing. You can't mess this up like you did at Rachel's wedding.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I was pregnant!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: And at Chandler's sister's wedding, you showed up late, drunk, and in a man's tuxedo.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I thought it was a costume party!

jokes.text: Rachel: 'Because I cared enough to lie.' — as her justification for being maid of honor
jokes.setup: Phoebe challenges why Rachel should be maid of honor after being exposed as a liar
jokes.punchline: Rachel argues her lie proves she cares MORE — a completely backwards moral position delivered with total confidence
jokes.explanation: One of the funnier lines of the episode — Rachel's complete moral inversion delivered as logical conclusion. The confidence of the delivery is key. Highly economical and very Rachel.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Phoebe, you can't just lie about being maid of honor!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Why not? It shows I care enough to make something up. That's way more work than just telling the truth.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: That's not... that's not how this works!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Fine, fine. But when you're giving your speech and you're crying, just remember — my fake stories would've been way better.

jokes.text: Phoebe: 'Coins hate me.'
jokes.setup: Rachel suggests flipping a coin to decide who's maid of honor
jokes.punchline: Phoebe refuses on the grounds that 'coins hate me' — an utterly Phoebe-specific irrational belief
jokes.explanation: Three words that are quintessentially Phoebe. The joke is entirely in the specificity — not 'I'm unlucky with coins' but coins as sentient beings with personal vendetta against her. Maximum economy, maximum character. High quotability and one of the clearest examples of voice-specific comedy in the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: It's like an audition, you know? You go in, you read the sides, you show 'em what you got.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: But here's the thing - I've been auditioning for years, and let me tell you, it is brutal. Do you know how many callbacks I've gotten? Zero. Absolute zero.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: I went to this one audition last week, right? For a hemorrhoid commercial. A hemorrhoid commercial! And I didn't get it. How do you not get a hemorrhoid commercial?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: And don't even get me started on the survival jobs. I've dressed up as a giant salami, I've done shower scenes where I cry... I mean, really cried.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: So my advice to you? Don't act. Don't ever do it. It'll destroy your soul and empty your bank account.

jokes.text: Rachel walks up to Ross with exaggerated sweetness: 'Ross, sweetie.' Joey follows: 'Hey there, handsome thing.'
jokes.setup: Rachel and Phoebe need Ross and Joey to judge their maid-of-honor audition
jokes.punchline: Joey mimics Rachel's coy flattery with 'Hey there, handsome thing' — the absurdity of Joey trying to flirt with Ross
jokes.explanation: Joey's oblivious mimicry of Rachel's flirtatious approach is well-executed physical/verbal comedy. The joke is in Joey's total unawareness that this reads differently from him than from Rachel.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: We could flip a coin to decide.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: No! Coins are against me. They always land on the side I don't want.

jokes.text: Joey compliments Ross's cologne: 'Wow, this cologne really is every bit as good as Giorgio.'
jokes.setup: Joey is trying to flatter Ross to get him to agree to judge the audition
jokes.punchline: His compliment is that Ross's cologne is 'every bit as good as Giorgio' — an oddly specific and slightly backhanded assessment
jokes.explanation: The specificity of 'Giorgio' is funny — Joey's flattery includes an unnecessary comparison that reveals his ceiling for compliments. Decent but not exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Ross, that cologne you're wearing? It's like if a forest had a PhD in chemistry and decided to smell like success.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm pretty sure it's illegal in several countries because it's too powerful. Women are literally walking into walls trying to follow the scent.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: If they bottled this and sold it, world peace would happen by Thursday.

jokes.text: Joey brings up the nap; Ross flatly denies: 'No. No, we don't.' Then Joey: 'That was the best nap I ever had.'
jokes.setup: Joey wants to talk about the nap; Ross is determined to never acknowledge it
jokes.punchline: Joey's earnest declaration that it was 'the best nap I ever had' is delivered with total sincerity against Ross's wall of denial
jokes.explanation: The clash between Ross's terror and Joey's innocent enthusiasm is the engine of this subplot. Joey's complete lack of embarrassment makes it funnier — he's not trying to be provocative, he genuinely loved the nap.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: That nap was amazing. I've never felt more comfortable with another man in my life.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Your shoulder, your body heat... it was perfect.

jokes.text: Ross: 'I've had better.' Joey: 'Okay, when?' Ross: 'All right! All right! It was the best nap ever!'
jokes.setup: Joey challenges Ross to name a better nap
jokes.punchline: Ross cannot name one, and breaks down admitting it was the best nap ever — the last thing he wanted to admit
jokes.explanation: The structure here is excellent: Ross makes a defensive claim, Joey calls the bluff with one word ('When?'), and the entire facade crumbles. The escalation from denial to full confession in three beats is tight and well-executed. Ross's volume on the admission sells it.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What do you have to drink?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh, I got some sleep aids, some more sleep aids, and... more sleep aids.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Joey, that's all sleep medication.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah, well, a guy's gotta nap.

jokes.text: Joey: 'I want to do it again.'
jokes.setup: Ross has dramatically declared the nap situation 'over'
jokes.punchline: Joey's quiet, earnest 'I want to do it again' — delivered with zero shame — lands like a romantic confession
jokes.explanation: Five words, perfectly placed. The joke works on multiple levels: it subverts Ross's dramatic 'it's over' immediately, it's delivered with complete sincerity, and it mimics romantic comedy language while being entirely about a nap. Joey's character — guileless, sensation-driven, unashamed — makes this land perfectly. One of the best lines of the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, I just realized who you remind me of.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Who?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: My dad. The way you reject women? It's exactly like how my dad rejected my mom.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I do not reject women like your father rejected your mother.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Yes, you do! You're doing it right now with Julie. You're pulling away, you're making excuses, you're—

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Okay, okay. So what are you saying? That I have some deep-seated fear of commitment that stems from watching your parents' dysfunction?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm saying that watching you with Julie is like watching a rerun of my childhood.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, that's... deeply disturbing.

jokes.text: Joey offers Ross a drink to smooth things over; his options are 'Warm milk and Excedrin PM'
jokes.setup: Joey tries to be a good host and offers Ross a drink after their tense exchange
jokes.punchline: His drink menu consists entirely of sleep-inducing items — milk and sleeping pills — clearly strategically chosen
jokes.explanation: Layered joke: on the surface, Joey offering sleep aids as beverages is absurd. But the implication is that Joey is literally trying to maneuver Ross into another nap — which makes it both funnier and very Joey. The specificity of 'Excedrin PM' elevates it above generic. Strong earned-vs-cheap score.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Do you know why Louis rejected me?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, I'm gonna guess it had something to do with you telling him your entire life story on the first date.

jokes.text: Julie confronts Chandler: 'You're Louis Posen.' Chandler: 'Who?' — He tries to figure out who he is mid-scene
jokes.setup: Julie approaches Chandler with recognition and intensity: 'I just figured out who you are'
jokes.punchline: She names him Louis Posen — her childhood crush — not Chandler at all; Chandler has no idea who that is
jokes.explanation: Light misdirection — the intensity of 'I figured out who you are' implies dramatic recognition, but she means a completely different person. Functional but not exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Julie, I'm sorry. I've been a jerk. I'm going to change. I'm going to be a better person.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: But I have to warn you - the better I become, the more you're going to realize what a terrible mistake you made dating me in the first place.

jokes.text: Julie's childhood friend rejected her because she was 'too fa... Ahh'
jokes.setup: Julie mirrors Chandler's situation — her best friend in fifth grade rejected her for a similar reason
jokes.punchline: She uses the EXACT same 'fa... Ahh' truncation that Chandler used — the running gag extends to a new character
jokes.explanation: The running gag spreading to a new character who wasn't present for the original is a clever structural move. The audience recognizes the pattern immediately and the laugh of recognition is earned. Good callback execution.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Okay, so you got your ones through tens, right?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Right, and it's simple. A ten is a ten.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Exactly! And a nine is just one less than a ten.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Which makes it a nine.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: See? You're getting it!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: So what's a five?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Well, a five is right in the middle.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: The middle of what?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Between a one and a ten, obviously.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Right. So that's why it's a five.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Now you got it!

jokes.text: Chandler: 'I'll do it. But I warn you, this may make me a better person. And that is not the man you fell in love with.'
jokes.setup: Monica pushes Chandler to apologize to Julie; he resists but agrees
jokes.punchline: His warning that becoming 'a better person' might ruin their relationship — delivered as genuine concern
jokes.explanation: One of the best Chandler lines in the episode. His self-deprecation has evolved into a genuinely clever paradox: the apology might make him better, and his Monica-loves-him-as-a-mess logic is both funny and weirdly sweet. 'That is not the man you fell in love with' is a great button.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: If you're having cold feet about the wedding, that's totally normal. Just take a deep breath and remember why you're doing this.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: But also, make sure your fiancé isn't going to run off with someone else, or get drunk and marry a stripper in Vegas, or suddenly decide they're not ready for commitment right before the ceremony.

jokes.text: Joey: 'One being the highest.' Ross: 'Ten is the highest.' Joey: 'Why is 10 the highest?' Ross: 'Because it's the highest.'
jokes.setup: Joey is explaining the scoring system for the maid-of-honor audition
jokes.punchline: Joey genuinely believes 1 is the highest; Ross corrects him; Joey challenges the logic; Ross can only answer 'because it's the highest'
jokes.explanation: Joey's innumeracy/illogic meets Ross's inability to explain basic concepts simply. The circular 'because it's the highest' response is a funny collapse — Ross can't actually explain why 10 is higher than 1 in a satisfying way, which makes him look almost as dumb as Joey.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, you want a drunk uncle? I'll give you a drunk uncle.

dialogue.speaker: Judge
dialogue.line: Wow, that was incredibly committed!

dialogue.speaker: Judge
dialogue.line: The way you tackled him was so authentic.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, I grew up with a lot of uncles.

jokes.text: In the maid-of-honor scenario, 'Monica' (Rachel) says she'll never get to sleep with Joey — Rachel breaks character to look at Joey
jokes.setup: Rachel is acting out Monica having cold feet; she improvises Monica's fears
jokes.punchline: One of Monica's fears is 'I'll never get to sleep with Joey' — the absurdity of this being a real concern
jokes.explanation: The joke works because Rachel is playing Monica while also clearly enjoying taking a dig at the actual Monica, and the Joey-as-object-of-desire angle is a callback to his character's established magnetism. The meta-layer (Rachel enjoying this too much) adds to it.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Phoebe, you can't just make a scene like that in public!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh yeah? You want to see a scene? I'll show you a scene. I know 47 ways to kill a man with my bare hands.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: What?

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: And that's just with my hands. You want to see what I can do with a cocktail sword?

jokes.text: Rachel's maid-of-honor speech includes: 'Also, I ran out on a wedding. You don't get to keep the gifts.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is giving advice to Monica about cold feet, drawing on personal experience
jokes.punchline: Her personal experience is running out on a wedding, and the specific practical warning is about the gifts
jokes.explanation: Excellent character-specific joke. The fact that Rachel's wisdom about cold feet comes from running away from Barry is perfect character history use. The specific practical concern — the gifts — is a perfect Rachel touch: even in a serious moment, she's thinking about material things. The conciseness is great.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey Ross, what if I told you that I just found out I'm actually a millionaire?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, that would be... statistically improbable given your current employment situation, and I would need to see documented evidence of said funds before accepting such a claim as factual.

jokes.text: Joey: 'Very good, drawing on your own experience. Very good.'
jokes.setup: Rachel has just said she ran out on a wedding as 'experience' that makes her a good maid of honor
jokes.punchline: Joey judges this positively as if 'running away from your own wedding' is a legitimate maid-of-honor credential
jokes.explanation: Joey as a completely unqualified judge delivering legitimate-sounding feedback is a good bit. His earnest approval of objectively bad experience credentials is funny.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Hi everyone. For those of you who don't know me, I'm Rachel Green, and I've been Monica's best friend for...

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Wait, no. That's the worst opening ever. Let me start over.

jokes.text: Phoebe responds to being called next with 'Yes, Your Honor'
jokes.setup: Joey calls for Phoebe to take her turn in the audition
jokes.punchline: Phoebe addresses Joey as 'Your Honor' — playing up the courtroom/judging metaphor with earnest formality
jokes.explanation: Light wordplay — not especially original but Phoebe's earnest commitment to the metaphor is charming. The joke is in the sincerity.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I met Monica when I was 6, and she was already basically a fully formed adult. Then I met Chandler at 25, and he had the maturity of a 6-year-old.

jokes.text: Phoebe calls Ross 'Your Honor' as she readies for her scenario.
jokes.setup: Phoebe steps forward for her audition scenario
jokes.punchline: She addresses Ross as 'Your Honor' — treating the informal judging as a courtroom
jokes.explanation: A quick, minor gag — Phoebe's oblivious sincerity makes it land, but it's a small moment.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I'm so excited about Monica's wedding. I've been anticipating this moment for so long, thinking about how beautiful it will be, how emotional...

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: ...and then I imagine Monica in that dress, and all I can think about is how hard Monica's gonna get railed on her wedding night!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Oh yeah!

jokes.text: Phoebe's solution to the drunk uncle: she runs up and screams at him, disrupting the entire ceremony
jokes.setup: Joey's scenario: Monica is about to say 'I do' when a drunk uncle starts yelling. 'What do you do?'
jokes.punchline: Phoebe doesn't try to calm the uncle — she just runs up and screams louder, creating a bigger scene
jokes.explanation: Perfectly Phoebe — her instinct to match chaos with more chaos is brilliant character comedy. The 'You want a little taste of Pheebs?' follow-up solidifies that she's fully committed to this strategy. The judges' immediate approval is a great topper.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Hi, I'm Chandler Bing. We met at that party?

dialogue.speaker: Julie
dialogue.line: Oh! You're Chandler 'The Funny Guy' Bing!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Actually, it's just Chandler Bing. The funny guy part isn't really... that's not a thing.

dialogue.speaker: Julie
dialogue.line: No, that's what everyone called you. 'Could Chandler BE any funnier?'

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh God.

jokes.text: Joey: 'Very good! Perfect score.' Ross: 'She just made a scene in the middle of the ceremony!'
jokes.setup: Phoebe has just screamed over a drunk uncle at a wedding ceremony
jokes.punchline: Joey gives her a perfect score; Ross points out she made the situation worse
jokes.explanation: Joey and Ross as the worst possible judges — one rewarding chaos, one being the voice of reason while trapped in an absurd situation — is a good dynamic. The contrast between their reactions sells the moment.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You want to know where 'Skidmark' came from?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, no!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I was just going to—

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I don't want to hear it!

jokes.text: Rachel begins her maid-of-honor speech with 'Webster's Dictionary defines marriage as...' then immediately cancels it: 'Okay, no! Forget that! That sucks!'
jokes.setup: Rachel is asked to give her maid-of-honor speech on the spot
jokes.punchline: She starts with the most clichéd wedding speech opener possible, then immediately calls it out as terrible and abandons it mid-sentence
jokes.explanation: Meta joke about the worst wedding speech cliché — the dictionary definition opener — that the show knows is terrible and flags it immediately. The self-aware rejection is funnier than just doing the cliché would be. The flustered recovery adds to it.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I'm really sorry about what I said about... you know, your weight.

dialogue.speaker: Julie
dialogue.line: My weight? What are you talking about?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I just thought... I mean, I assumed you knew why I...

dialogue.speaker: Julie
dialogue.line: Oh my God. You broke up with me because of my weight and didn't even tell me?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, when you say it like that, it sounds bad.

jokes.text: Rachel: '...and became friends with Chandler when he was 25, although he seemed like a 6-year-old.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is giving a heartfelt speech about knowing Monica and Chandler
jokes.punchline: She slips in a dig at Chandler's maturity while maintaining the tone of a sincere toast
jokes.explanation: Light dig at Chandler that works because it's delivered mid-sincere-speech. The contrast between the heartfelt framing and the insult is well-timed.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, I've successfully made things worse. Mission accomplished.

jokes.text: Phoebe's speech: 'I remember talking about this day with Rachel while we were showering together, naked.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe gives what starts as a sincere speech about anticipating Monica's wedding
jokes.punchline: She closes with 'while we were showering together, naked' — both TMI and an oddly specific detail that torpedoes the sincerity
jokes.explanation: Classic Phoebe overshare. The word 'naked' at the end of an otherwise sincere speech is perfectly placed for maximum audience reaction. The addition of 'naked' after 'showering together' is redundant and therefore even funnier — Phoebe clarifying what showering involves. High impact for a broad audience.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: There are no losers in this competition.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Well, except Rachel.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: What?!

jokes.text: Joey: 'And she's back in the game!'
jokes.setup: Phoebe appeared to be losing the maid-of-honor competition until her 'naked' speech
jokes.punchline: Joey's sports-announcer reaction to Phoebe's recovery
jokes.explanation: Joey treating a maid-of-honor audition like a sporting event is a good character beat. The energy and economy of 'and she's back in the game!' works as a button.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: The competition was really close.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: No it wasn't.

jokes.text: Julie greets Chandler with 'Hello, Skidmark.'
jokes.setup: Chandler nervously introduces himself to Julie, expecting hostility
jokes.punchline: She calls him 'Skidmark' — an unexpectedly specific and degrading nickname
jokes.explanation: One word does all the work. 'Skidmark' is unexpected, specific, funny on its own, and implies a whole humiliating backstory that the audience will fill in. Maximum economy — the joke is entirely in the choice of that word. High quotability.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God, I won! Finally! You know what this means? The inanimate objects have ended their grudge against me. We can all move forward now.

jokes.text: Chandler: 'It's a nickname. I'll explain later.' Monica: 'It's pretty clear.'
jokes.setup: Julie calls Chandler 'Skidmark' in front of Monica
jokes.punchline: Monica's flat 'It's pretty clear' — she doesn't need an explanation; the nickname speaks for itself
jokes.explanation: Monica's deadpan follow-up is a perfect button to the Skidmark joke. The implication is that Monica immediately understands exactly why he was called Skidmark, which says something about Chandler. Very economical.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: It's going to be very Phoebe — lots of crystals, maybe some chanting, probably a goat.

jokes.text: Chandler apologizes for breaking up with Julie 'because you were overweight.' Julie: 'That's why you broke up with me?' — she didn't know
jokes.setup: Chandler delivers his long-overdue apology, believing Julie already knew the reason
jokes.punchline: Julie had no idea — she thought the reason was something else — so his apology reveals a secret she didn't have
jokes.explanation: Classic sitcom irony executed with great structure: Chandler's apology, meant to fix things, reveals a NEW wound. The setup is well-constructed — we see the apology scene coming and expect resolution — but the twist is a great subversion. His 'You didn't know that?' follow-up makes it worse in the best way.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: She gained some weight.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: How much weight?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, let's just say she's gone from the Miss Universe Pageant to the Miss Universe Pizza Hut.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God! That's not funny!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Okay, maybe a little funny. But still not funny!

jokes.text: Chandler: 'You didn't know that?' — realizing he's just made everything worse
jokes.setup: Julie's confused reaction reveals she didn't know why Chandler broke up with her
jokes.punchline: Chandler asks 'You didn't know that?' — a moment of dawning horror as he realizes he's just delivered a fresh insult
jokes.explanation: The realization beat is perfectly timed. Chandler's 'You didn't know that?' is delivered as pure confused horror and it's the precise moment the audience understands the full disaster he's created. Great cringe beat.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You called me fat at Thanksgiving!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I was kidding!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No you weren't.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Okay, fine. But I said it behind your back, so it doesn't count.

jokes.text: Chandler: 'Well, I guess my work here is done.' — after having massively worsened the situation
jokes.setup: Chandler has just accidentally revealed a new insult to Julie while trying to apologize
jokes.punchline: He declares his work done as if the apology went well — classic Chandler retreat-via-sarcasm
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler escape hatch — when in a hole, declare victory and walk away. The irony is total and character-consistent. Good economy.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I was just thinking, you know, relationships are all about compromise and— wait, why do I always say things that make no sense? I literally just watched myself say that and thought, 'that guy's an idiot.' Which is me. I'm watching myself be an idiot in real time. Could I BE any more self-aware about my complete lack of self-awareness?

jokes.text: Joey: 'I'd also like to say, in this competition, there are no losers. Well, except Rachel. Damn it!'
jokes.setup: Joey begins a diplomatic 'no losers' speech about the maid-of-honor audition
jokes.punchline: He immediately contradicts himself — 'Well, except Rachel' — then curses at his own lack of tact
jokes.explanation: Perfect Joey structure: attempt at diplomacy → immediate self-sabotage → self-aware frustration. The 'Damn it!' at his own mistake is what elevates this from a simple insult to a character-driven joke. The sequence has three beats and all three land.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Would you love me if I shrank to 2 inches tall?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Of course I would. I'd put you in my pocket and take you everywhere with me.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: That's sweet.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah, and I'd introduce you to people as my tiny wife. 'This is my wife Monica. She's two inches tall.' And then I'd take you out and show you off at parties.

jokes.text: Joey: 'Actually, it wasn't that close.' — immediately after Ross says it was
jokes.setup: Ross tries to soften the blow by saying the competition 'was really close'
jokes.punchline: Joey immediately contradicts: 'Actually, it wasn't that close.'
jokes.explanation: Joey's total inability to read the social situation and his immediate contradiction of Ross's diplomatic lie is a clean, efficient joke. The timing (immediately after Ross) makes it land harder.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm sorry for being such a baby.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God, you're a baby? I didn't know that! How is that even possible?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: No, Phoebe, I meant—

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Wait, wait. You're not actually a baby? Oh. Oh! You mean like... emotionally!

jokes.text: Phoebe wins the coin flip and declares: 'The coins have finally forgiven me!'
jokes.setup: Phoebe earlier said 'coins hate me' and refused a coin flip
jokes.punchline: After winning the flip, she celebrates that 'the coins have finally forgiven me' — treating coins as beings with grudges and mercy
jokes.explanation: The callback to 'coins hate me' is perfect. The escalation from 'coins hate me' (coins as enemies) to 'the coins have finally forgiven me' (coins as forgiving entities) is a beautiful expansion of the original joke's internal logic. It deepens Phoebe's worldview consistently and the emotional relief she expresses is hilarious. One of the best jokes in the episode.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: She dressed up as a bride for Halloween, and Wonder Woman was carrying her train.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'You know what? I hope Monica forgives you after you throw her her vegetarian-voodoo-goddess-circle-y shower.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is a sore loser after losing the maid-of-honor decision
jokes.punchline: Her parting shot is a compound insult about Phoebe's inevitable hippie-themed shower
jokes.explanation: 'Vegetarian-voodoo-goddess-circle-y' is a funny specific compound adjective that captures exactly what a Phoebe-planned event would look like. Good character-specific insult. Slightly over-hyphenated but it works.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: You've been thinking about this since you were 14.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Since I was 10.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God!

jokes.text: Joey: 'Boy, I tell you. That judging stuff took a lot out of me.'
jokes.setup: The audition is over; Joey reflects on his experience
jokes.punchline: Joey treats sitting and watching two people give speeches as an exhausting ordeal
jokes.explanation: Light Joey laziness joke. Functions as a setup for his nap scheme rather than standing entirely on its own.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Okay Phoebe, I'm gonna be honest with you. Monica's been planning this wedding for like three months, and I've sat through approximately eight thousand meetings about napkin colors and chair arrangements.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: You're about to enter a world of pain. A world of Monica-level organizational intensity.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: My advice? Just smile, nod, and pray she doesn't make a spreadsheet about your bridesmaids' shoe sizes.

jokes.text: Joey casually mentions he's going upstairs to nap on his couch, then looks at Ross meaningfully
jokes.setup: Joey and Ross's nap situation — both want to do it again but Ross won't admit it
jokes.punchline: Joey's completely transparent attempt to lure Ross into another nap by simply announcing where he'll be
jokes.explanation: Joey's transparent scheme — just announcing the location like a romantic invitation — mirrors the nap-as-romance metaphor established earlier. His 'that's where I'll be' with meaningful weight is a good escalation of the running gag.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh my God!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I can't believe it. I'm gonna have to tell everyone about this.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: No, no, no, Chandler, it's not what it looks like!

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Yeah man, we were just napping!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Sure you were.

jokes.text: Chandler's reflection: 'As bad as that went, I actually enjoyed myself. I think I'm going to apologize for all the stupid things I do.'
jokes.setup: Chandler has just catastrophically worsened Julie's pain with his apology
jokes.punchline: He's learned the wrong lesson — not to stop doing stupid things but to enjoy apologizing for them
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler growth-without-change joke. He's taken a catastrophic apology and found a way to make it a positive personality trait. The character consistency is good.

jokes.text: Monica: 'Why don't you just stop doing stupid things? Then you wouldn't have to apologize.' Chandler: 'I'd love it if I could do both.'
jokes.setup: Monica suggests the logical solution: stop doing stupid things
jokes.punchline: Chandler treats 'doing both' (continuing stupid things AND apologizing for them) as the ideal outcome
jokes.explanation: 'I'd love it if I could do both' is a great line — Chandler's ideal life involves continuing bad behavior with the option of apologizing afterward. It's self-aware self-destruction and deeply character-specific. Clean, economical structure.

jokes.text: Monica asks Chandler how much weight Julie gained; he says a hundred and forty-five pounds. Monica: 'In one year? My God, what did she eat? Her family?'
jokes.setup: Chandler defends his teenage behavior; Monica asks how much weight Julie gained to contextualize it
jokes.punchline: 145 pounds in one year → Monica asks 'What did she eat? Her family?' — dark, specific, delivered with genuine shock
jokes.explanation: 'What did she eat? Her family?' is a dark, punchy line that gets a big laugh because it's simultaneously horrified and morbidly specific. Monica's shock is genuine, making the dark humor land harder. High quotability.

jokes.text: Monica asks what Julie gained. Chandler: 'A hundred and forty-five pounds.' Monica: 'In one year? My God, what did she eat? Her family?'
jokes.setup: Monica is probing how much weight Julie gained, trying to contextualize Chandler's breakup.
jokes.punchline: 'What did she eat? Her family?' — Monica's dark, escalating horror at the number lands with a great cannibalism punchline.
jokes.explanation: The escalation from 'In one year?' (surprise) to 'My God' (horror) to 'what did she eat? Her family?' (dark absurdism) is very well-structured. The cannibalism turn is unexpected and dark enough to get a big laugh. Monica's reaction here is especially funny given her personal history with weight, adding an ironic layer. 'Her family?' is the perfect punchline — specific enough to be visual, dark enough to be surprising.

jokes.text: Monica reveals Chandler called her fat during Thanksgiving — but his defense is: 'You were not supposed to hear that. I said that behind your back.'
jokes.setup: Monica confronts Chandler about calling her fat at Thanksgiving
jokes.punchline: Chandler's defense is that she wasn't supposed to hear it — the implicit logic being that it's only wrong if you get caught
jokes.explanation: One of the best lines of the episode. The logic is completely wrong but delivered as though it's reasonable — 'I said it behind your back' as a defense, as if that makes it acceptable. The audience understands exactly how wrong this is while Chandler presents it with sincerity. High quotability, strong structure.

jokes.text: Chandler: 'You have to realize I don't think of you as a thin, beautiful woman.'
jokes.setup: Chandler is trying to reassure Monica he loves her regardless of weight
jokes.punchline: His reassurance begins with what sounds like an insult: 'I don't think of you as a thin, beautiful woman'
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler saying something that sounds bad before it becomes good. The misdirection works because it hangs for a beat before the clarification. His acknowledgment 'This is one of the things I can apologize for later' is a good self-aware button.

jokes.text: Chandler: 'This is one of the things that I can apologize for later.'
jokes.setup: Chandler has just said 'I don't think of you as a thin, beautiful woman' mid-reassurance
jokes.punchline: He calls back his own earlier joke about apologizing for stupid things — right as he's doing a stupid thing
jokes.explanation: Perfect callback — Chandler immediately demonstrates his new philosophy (keep doing dumb things, apologize later) in real time. The self-awareness is both funny and weirdly endearing. The callback is tight and pays off the earlier setup beautifully.

jokes.text: Chandler reacts to his own bad phrasing: 'This is one of the things that I can apologize for later.'
jokes.setup: Chandler has just accidentally said Monica isn't a 'thin, beautiful woman' and realizes it mid-sentence.
jokes.punchline: He immediately categorizes this as future apology material — referencing his earlier plan to apologize for stupid things — which is both a callback and a funny self-aware acknowledgment of his own mistake.
jokes.explanation: A satisfying callback to the apologizing subplot. Chandler's self-categorization of this new mistake as 'one of the things I can apologize for later' is funny because he's already doing the thing he was going to stop doing, and he knows it, and he's planning for it. Meta and character-specific.

jokes.text: Monica: 'Even if I shrink down to 2 inches tall?' Chandler: 'I'd carry you around in my pocket.'
jokes.setup: Monica is testing Chandler's declaration of unconditional love
jokes.punchline: She takes 'shrink down' literally to 2 inches, and Chandler's response is entirely practical and sweet: pocket-carrying
jokes.explanation: Cute absurdist beat — Monica testing the edge of the unconditional love declaration with a 2-inch scenario. Chandler's immediate practical answer (pocket) is both funny and sweet. Lands as a romantic moment with a comedy topping.

jokes.text: Julie, hearing Chandler's pocket line to Monica, mutters: 'Skidmark still got a way with the ladies.'
jokes.setup: Julie witnesses Chandler's sweet moment with Monica
jokes.punchline: She grudgingly acknowledges his charm, but delivers it with the 'Skidmark' callback — the affection and the insult coexist
jokes.explanation: A satisfying button to the Julie subplot. The 'Skidmark' callback makes it land harder than if she'd used his name. The ambivalent acknowledgment of his charm is a nice character note.

jokes.text: Rachel apologizes for 'being a baby.' Phoebe: 'That's ridiculous. Rachel, we were all babies once.' — before realizing she means 'today'
jokes.setup: Rachel apologizes for acting like 'a baby' about the maid-of-honor situation
jokes.punchline: Phoebe takes it literally — babies, the infant kind — before Rachel corrects her
jokes.explanation: Very Phoebe — she takes a figure of speech literally. The timing of Rachel clarifying 'Oh, you mean today. Yeah.' is a good button. Functional character comedy.

jokes.text: Rachel explains she's wanted to be Monica's maid of honor since she was 10. 'I just developed early.'
jokes.setup: Phoebe says Rachel has been thinking about this since she was 'what, 14?'
jokes.punchline: Rachel corrects her: she was 10, adding 'I just developed early' — an unexpected non-sequitur about physical development dropped into an emotional conversation
jokes.explanation: 'I just developed early' is a great non-sequitur that lands in the middle of a touching moment. It's both a characteristic Rachel overshare and a funny misdirect — the clarification adds nothing relevant but everything comedically.

jokes.text: Joey reacts to 'I just developed early' with an astonished 'Man alive!'
jokes.setup: Rachel mentions she 'developed early'
jokes.punchline: Joey's breathless 'Man alive!' — an involuntary, almost awe-struck reaction
jokes.explanation: Two words, complete character encapsulation. Joey's involuntary reaction to Rachel's 'developed early' comment is pure Joey libido. 'Man alive!' is a funny, slightly archaic expression that makes it funnier than a straight reaction would be.

jokes.text: Monica reveals her wedding-planning demands: 'We should meet four times a week... 6:30, my place. So excited!'
jokes.setup: Rachel has just won the maid-of-honor role
jokes.punchline: Monica's excitement immediately translates to an overwhelming, controlling schedule
jokes.explanation: Classic Monica control-freak moment. The speed at which she escalates from 'great!' to 'four times a week at 6:30' is a good character beat. Functions well as a payoff to Rachel winning the role.

jokes.text: Phoebe to Rachel after Monica walks away: 'Yeah, okay. You laugh now. She's gonna be yours.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is enjoying Phoebe's predicament of being Monica's maid of honor
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's knowing 'She's gonna be yours' — when Phoebe gets married, Monica's intensity will be Rachel's problem
jokes.explanation: Good callback to the rotating maid-of-honor system established in the opening. Phoebe delivering a threat/promise in the same breath is a satisfying button to the A-plot.

jokes.text: Ross and Joey are discovered asleep together on the couch again, in the same position
jokes.setup: Ross resisted Joey's transparent nap invitation; the scene cuts to them asleep together
jokes.punchline: Despite all resistance, Ross is exactly where Joey predicted — on the couch, napping together
jokes.explanation: The payoff to the entire B-plot. The joke is entirely structural — the audience knows Ross couldn't resist, and the confirmation gets a huge laugh. The lack of dialogue is the point: no explanation needed. The visual of them together again is the punchline. This is a classic multi-camera sitcom button that plays perfectly to a live audience.

jokes.text: Joey wakes up to find Rachel watching them: 'Great nap.' Ross: 'It really was.'
jokes.setup: Rachel has caught Ross and Joey napping together
jokes.punchline: Instead of denial this time, Ross and Joey both peacefully confirm it was a great nap — Ross has fully surrendered
jokes.explanation: Perfect character arc resolution in four words. Ross started the episode with 'We fell asleep. That is all. Never speak of this.' and has arrived at peaceful 'It really was.' The surrender is total and the economy is extraordinary. This is the best punchline in the episode — it pays off the entire B-plot arc with zero waste. High rewatch bonus because the full journey makes it even better.

jokes.text: Ross and Joey's friend catches them napping and panics: 'Dude, what the hell are you doing? God!'
jokes.setup: Ross and Joey are peacefully asleep together; a third character (Chandler presumably) discovers them
jokes.punchline: The shocked reaction mirrors the audience's first exposure to the situation — the gag resets with fresh horror
jokes.explanation: The final escalation — a fresh set of eyes on the nap situation. Having a new character react with the same horror Ross and Joey had in the opening creates a satisfying ring structure. The episode ends on this note, which is a strong button.

tmdb_overview: Joey and Ross accidentally take a nap together - and much to their dismay, find that they liked it. Phoebe and Rachel compete to become Monica's maid of honor.
insight: Chandler-Monica dynamic anchors 56 jokes at 2.77-per-minute clip for season high.
